title: Coastal Curry Brings South Indian Flavors to Scarborough, Maine
excerpt: Owners Kiran Kumar Vellanki and David Patel opened Coastal Curry on August 15, specializing in Hyderabadi Dum Biryani and dosas alongside North Indian favorites.
body:
• Coastal Curry opened Saturday, August 15, at 300 Gallery Blvd in Scarborough, Maine, bringing South Indian specialties like Hyderabadi Dum Biryani and dosas to Southern Maine.
  • The restaurant is owned by Kiran Kumar Vellanki and David Patel, and serves both South and North Indian cuisine seven days a week.
  • Coastal Curry joins a growing wave of Indian restaurants in the greater Portland area, including Bombay Bistro in Westbrook, Aromas of India at the Maine Mall, and the established Taj Indian Cuisine in South Portland.

Southern Maine's Indian dining scene continues to expand. Coastal Curry, a new restaurant specializing in South Indian cuisine, opened its doors on Saturday, August 15, at 300 Gallery Blvd in Scarborough — a strip that sits adjacent to the Super Walmart on Gallery Boulevard.

The restaurant is the project of co-owners Kiran Kumar Vellanki and David Patel, who have built the menu around South Indian staples that remain underrepresented in Maine's restaurant landscape. Hyderabadi Dum Biryani — the slow-cooked, layered rice dish synonymous with the city of Hyderabad — anchors the offerings alongside a range of dosas, the crisp fermented-rice crepes that are a dietary staple across South India.

South Indian Focus, North Indian Breadth

"South Indian Focus, North Indian Breadth While the South Indian dishes are the draw, Coastal Curry also offers popular North Indian items to ensure broad appeal."

While the South Indian dishes are the draw, Coastal Curry also offers popular North Indian items to ensure broad appeal. The dual approach reflects a model that has worked well for Indian restaurants entering markets where diners may be more familiar with tikka masala and naan than with sambar and rasam.

The restaurant occupies the space formerly home to Clean Eatz and plans to operate seven days a week: Monday through Thursday from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and 4:30 to 10 p.m., and Friday through Sunday from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., according to Portland Food Map.

A Growing Scene

Coastal Curry's arrival is part of a broader trend in Southern Maine. Several Indian restaurants have opened across the region in recent years. Bombay Bistro took over the former Frog & Turtle space in Westbrook. Aromas of India set up in the Maine Mall food court in South Portland, filling the spot that Arby's once occupied. Taj Indian Cuisine, a long-established South Portland fixture known for its daily lunch buffet and extensive menu of South and North Indian dishes, continues to draw steady crowds. India Palace on Congress Street in Portland serves North Indian and Himalayan fare.

The expanding restaurant footprint mirrors the broader growth of the Indian-origin community in New England. Maine's Indian population, while still modest compared to metropolitan hubs like Boston or New York, has grown steadily as tech companies, healthcare systems, and universities in the greater Portland area have attracted professionals and their families.

What to Know Before You Go

For diaspora families in the region, a South Indian-focused restaurant is a notable addition. Hyderabadi Dum Biryani — made with basmati rice layered with marinated meat, saffron, and slow-cooked in a sealed pot — and properly made dosas with coconut chutney and sambar are dishes that many Indian-Americans drive considerable distances to find. Coastal Curry's location in Scarborough, roughly 10 minutes south of downtown Portland, puts it within easy reach of Portland, South Portland, Cape Elizabeth, and Westbrook.

A Nepali-Tibetan restaurant, Himalayas on the Bay, also recently opened nearby in Knightville at 60 Ocean Street, further diversifying the South Asian dining options in the Portland metro area.
nri_angle: Coastal Curry fills a gap for Indian-Americans in Southern Maine seeking authentic South Indian dishes like Hyderabadi Dum Biryani and dosas closer to home.
